items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: I got to know a white gentleman by the name of Sim Black. He was scoutmaster of Boy Scout Troop Thirteen. And he used to visit our band quarters pretty regularly.

ctx.x: Do you remember about, excuse me, what year that was about? Was that...

That could have been about 1910. 1910, when you joined the Silver Leaf. Silver Leaf Band. I was still living in Jefferson Paris. And then I moved to New Orleans in 1911. And I was still with Silver Leaf Band. And Mr. Welch, he was a sickly man and he gave up the coinette playing. And we got over to the fellow by the name of Hippolyte Charles. He played coinette for us a while. And then he gave up the coinette playing and old man Welch came back again. And old man Welch made me to know Celestine. He said he was a…
You had already called it the Tuxedo Band though before you started the tuxedos. Is that right? Yes. And he was a big help to us.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Now the man that made a suggestion for us to call our band the original tuxedo, his name was Mr. Sim Black. He was a master of Boy Scout troop 13, and he thought a whole lot of our band.

ctx.x: For a club, one of the clubs that had you in the city of New Orleans, which is a colored club, and we wanted quadrillo. And we played for them. But I never didn't know much about playing a quadrillo. That wasn't in my time of playing music, you see. But I have seen them dance quadrillo before that, you see. I've seen them dance quadrillo. Now our tuxedo band, you see, many people want to know how the band got to be named the original tuxedo orchestra. See, we used to call it tuxedo band, well of course there…
Is Sim Black about your age?
